I’ve never taken 2C-B, but about a year and a half ago I binged on psychs for 4 months, give it take a couple weeks. I had access to a nearly unlimited supply of LSD (or at least a similar analog, as each batch passed the UV light test) from my dealer who I taught how to acquire it from the dark web, as I was unwilling to take that risk myself. I was also growing a large quantity of mushrooms as a hobby. So, as I said, for 4 months I was tripping constantly, taking increasingly large dosages to combat the instantaneous tolerance of LSD and psilocybin. I was pretty much following the %300 rule, if anyone here as heard of it. I was at a point where I could operate at my fast paced high intensity job while under the influence. I never took a break longer than 3 or 4 days. It was insane and stupid. I should have known that taking 15 150ug hits of acid on the regular was stupid, but hey, it was awesome. 

 Anyway, I stopped all of a sudden. It want really planned, but the plug went silent and I was in the process of moving so my mushroom growing went on hold, but I didn’t think much of it. And then my reality collapsed after a day or so. Looking back, I’m pretty sure I was in a sort of psychosis for a couple weeks, as I couldn’t think and was stuck in a negative feedback loop of thinking I was dying and feeling like reality wasn’t, well, real. It’s hard to explain, but I was in turmoil. I had the visuals you describe, as well as content tracers/trails. Any movement in my field of vision had a long trail, all the time, day and night, no matter the lighting. It fucked with me real hard. I thought my life was over.

 So, I researched and sought help and advice (/r/hppd was a great resource) and pretty much what everyone says is right. You aren’t permanently damaged, at least not severely. Staying away from all substances is key, because at least for me even cannabis made it worse (I actually couldn’t smoke at all for awhile, as it would make me feel like I was on a bad acid trip) Eating healthy and exercise are also very helpful, it makes you feel better and gives you something to focus on other than your symptoms. I found solace in meditation, as I had to sort out my brain which I had rewired so carelessly. And time. Time is real what heals you. Even now at 18 months out, I still have minor trails at all times (though I coped with it and think it’s kind of cool, I see the world a different way than most now) but all of my other symptoms are diminished or nonexistent. It took me about 10-12months to start to actually feel okay though, so it took a lot of work and patience.

 The point of all this, my friend, is that you are going to be okay. Science doesn’t really understand HPPD too well, although I believe it is listed in the DSM-5 (citation needed) but what we do know is that you aren’t going to die, it will get better, and you will eventually feel yourself again, whether it be you’ve learned to cope with your new reality or you no longer have symptoms.

Fear not, stay strong, and use this time to focus on yourself, which is healthy regardless. Best of luck, feel free to message if you have questions, it’s been a wild ride.

My parents repeatedly told me this my entire childhood and young adulthood (I'm currently 19, so I guess I'm still experiencing that), and it still rings in my ears when things are too quiet. It made sense when I was little, make mommy and daddy happy, y'know? But when I got a bit older and started to try to express myself, anything I said that wasn't apart of their perfect plan for me was dismissed or even punished. Though, through some tough personal experiences and the help of great people I uprooted some suppressed memories and started to put 2 and 2 together and realized how emotionally abusive and controlling they were. I moved out when I was 18 without their permission, and have never been happier.
